findings.title: Update operational Rust parser limits in architecture and fitness guides
findings.trigger: An operator uses the architecture or local-fitness guide to choose admitted Rust files or interpret a parser-budget failure.
findings.impact: Both current guides say 32 KiB and 128 lexical units, including comments/literals, while the shared parser admits 400 KiB and 32768 tokens with depth/path limits and opaque comments/literals. Users can unnecessarily split or exclude ordinary files and misdiagnose which budget actually failed. The allocation-free wording also fails to describe the worker-stack resource boundary.
findings.evidence: Direct comparison of ARCHITECTURE.md74-79 and LOCAL_FITNESS.md37-41 with rust_parse.rs10-18 and RUST_PARSER_BOUNDS.md; deterministic source/document mismatch, no execution required.
findings.remediation: Replace obsolete limit paragraphs with the current bounds and a link to RUST_PARSER_BOUNDS.md. Preserve historical proof records as historical evidence.
findings.acceptance_relevance: Current operator-documentation accuracy; no future-v0.93 implementation requirement is inferred.
